34	  the base-changed genus `genus C_κ`.  This is the honest content of "the theorem re-fires per
35	  field", now stated at an object rather than about a class.
36	* `UniformVanishing` — the **open half, named as a definition** so that consumers can quantify
37	  over it and so that its exact quantifier order is inspectable: `∃ b, ∀ κ, ∀ D on C_κ, …`.
38	  The `b` is chosen **before** `κ`.  This is *not* proved here and this file does not claim it.
39	* `uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` — the **reduction**: the open half
40	  follows from exactly **two** inputs, a uniform degree bound on a vanishing base divisor and
41	  base-field invariance of the genus.  Neither is proved here; both are named precisely.
42	* `exists_deg_ge` — **non-vacuity**: degrees are unbounded above given one closed point of
43	  positive residue degree, so a degree half-space is never empty and `UniformVanishing` is not
44	  trivially satisfiable by having no instances.  Proved.
45	
46	## What the constant actually decomposes into (correcting my own earlier account)
47	
48	`FiberBound`'s closing docstring located the obstruction in the constant: `b(κ)` is built from
49	`n₀(κ)`, a `Classical.choose` on a Noetherian stabilization re-run at each base field, and
50	nothing relates `n₀(κ)` to `n₀(k)`.  That describes the *proof*, not the *problem*.  The
51	threshold produced by `DegreeVanishing.exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one` is
52	
53	`b = deg D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪)`,
54	
55	and that existential is **monotone in `b`** (a `D` of degree `≥ b'` has degree `≥ b` whenever
56	`b ≤ b'`).  So `n₀` itself never has to transport: it suffices to bound `b(κ)` above by
57	something independent of `κ`.  Since `χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = 1 − genus C_κ` (`ChiCurve.chi_moduleKSheaf`
58	composed with `GenusBridge.ledgerGenus_eq_genus`, both at `C_κ` — this is checked, not assumed),
59	
60	`b(κ) = deg_κ D₀(κ) + genus C_κ`,
61	
62	which exposes **two** `κ`-dependencies, not one:
63	
64	1. `genus C_κ` — a scalar, addressed by base-field invariance of the genus;
65	2. `deg_κ D₀(κ)` — the degree of the base divisor, where `D₀(κ) = n₀(κ) • F_κ`.  This is where
66	   the `Classical.choose` survives, and bounding it is *not* a corollary of (1).
67	
68	**A retraction.**  An earlier version of this docstring said the threshold "can be taken to be
69	`2g − 1`", which would have collapsed (2) into (1) and made the genus identity the whole
70	residue.  That is standard curve theory but it is **not available here**: `deg D ≥ 2g − 1 ⟹
71	H¹ = 0` goes through Serre duality, and there is **no Serre duality, canonical divisor or
72	dualizing sheaf anywhere in this workspace** — searched across AJC, AJCR and mathlib, which
73	has no Serre duality for curves at all.  So the reduction below carries both hypotheses.  I
74	had published the one-input version on the team thread before checking it; this is the
75	corrected form.
76	
77	## Where the two inputs stand (provenance, honestly)
78	
79	**Input (1), genus invariance: proved sorry-free next door, on a different carrier.**
80	`AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance.lean` in
81	Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild proves `finrank_h1_baseField` (the `κ`-dimension of
82	`H¹(C_κ, 𝒪)` equals the `k`-dimension of `H¹(C, 𝒪)`, arbitrary field extension) and deduces
83	`genus_baseField`.  Its engine is termwise base change of the two-term Čech complex of an
84	affine two-cover plus right-exactness of `⊗` — not semicontinuity, not Mumford II.5.
85	
86	**The carrier question is settled, and favourably.**  AJCR states it at `baseChangeBundle C K`,
87	built from its own `overSpec`/`⊗` `Over`-tensor spelling, whereas AJC's `C_κ` is
88	`Over.mk (pullback.snd C.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k κ))))`.  Those agree by
89	`rfl` — **the whole bundled object, structure morphism included**, not merely the underlying
90	scheme.  AJCR's `⊗` is the monoidal product in `Over (Spec k)`, whose `tensorObj` *is* the
91	pullback and whose `snd` *is* `pullback.snd`, so the difference is notational indirection.
92	
93	Verified at *this* project's spelling rather than taken on report, with a negative control: the
94	same `rfl` with the pullback arguments swapped fails on a type mismatch, so the check is not
95	proving whatever it is handed.  Two caveats survive, and neither is cosmetic:
96	
97	* the verdict is defeq **at the object**.  A port that pushes it through a functor must re-run
98	  `rfl` there; a lane in this workspace shipped a false claim this week by carrying an
99	  object-level verdict across `Spec.map`.
100	* defeq of carriers is necessary, not sufficient.  The genus statements also bind AJCR's own
101	  curve-instance stack (`Curve.BaseChangeInstances`) and its two-cover `curveCover`, and whether
102	  *those* land on AJC's `CurveBaseChange` instances is a separate measurement, not settled here.
103	
104	So the honest status of input (1) is: **reachable, cost not yet measured** — no longer "blocked on
105	a carrier mismatch", which is what I would have recorded had I stopped at the mismatch.  It stays
106	a hypothesis in the reduction below until the port is actually made, because an unmeasured port
107	is not an available theorem.
108	
109	**The AJC-native route to input (1), measured.**  Because the carriers agree, there is a second
110	option besides porting AJCR's file: assemble the identity from bricks AJC already owns.  What is
111	present, checked at HEAD:
112	
113	* a **cover on `C`**: `Adelic.LaurentChartData.pullbackSquare` (`Adelic/FinitenessP1.lean:439`)
114	  builds a `C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare` from the ℙ¹ chart data and any finite `π`, and
115	  `Ledger/MapToP1.exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1` supplies the `π` at AJC's curve;
116	* a **cover on `C_κ`**: `Scheme.AffineCoverMVSquare.baseChangeField` (`CurveBaseChange.lean:340`)
117	  transports it, since the first projection `C_κ ⟶ C` is affine;
118	* the **genus read on that cover**: `AffineCoverMVSquare.h1_unit_baseChangeField_eq_genus`
119	  (`CohomologyKit.lean:582`) already says `h¹(𝒪_{C_κ})` on the base-changed cover *is*
120	  `genus C_κ`, and `h0_unit_baseChangeField_eq_one` gives `h⁰ = 1`.
121	
122	So AJC has both sides of the comparison expressed on transported covers; what is **missing** is
123	the comparison itself — the termwise base-change equivalence `Γ(C, V) ⊗_k κ ≃ Γ(C_κ, V_κ)` on
124	chart sections, which is what AJCR's `relSectionsBaseChange` supplies and what makes `h¹` agree
125	rather than merely both being defined.  That equivalence is the actual deliverable, on either
126	route.  Note the shape of the two projects' cover carriers differs — AJCR uses `AffineTwoCover`,
127	AJC `AffineCoverMVSquare` (and `AffineTwoCover` does not occur anywhere in AJC) — so a port
128	crosses a second carrier boundary that the `rfl` above does *not* cover.
129	
130	**Input (2), a uniform base-divisor degree bound: open, and not located in either project.**
131	It asks for one `d` with a vanishing `D₀` of degree `≤ d` over *every* `κ`.  Nothing in AJC or
132	AJCR bounds `n₀(κ)` uniformly; AJCR's analogue is a `Nat.find` per field
133	(`RiemannRoch/WindowLedger.lean`), and its `WindowFieldTransport.lean` transports vanishing
134	*facts* one field at a time precisely because the constant does not move.
135	
136	So `uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` is a **conditional** result with one
137	antecedent that is proved-elsewhere-modulo-a-carrier and one that is genuinely open.
138	
139	## The three cluster-P statements, kept apart (unchanged discipline)
140	
141	1. **Single-field bounded vanishing** — closed at AJC's curve (`FiberBound`, three curve
142	   binders, nothing else).  This file changes nothing about it.
143	2. **Extension-uniformity** — free half now *witnessed* at `C_κ` (was: asserted of morphism
144	   classes); open half now *decomposed* into a genus identity plus a uniform base-divisor
145	   degree bound, with the second one named rather than folded into the first.  Still open.
146	3. **Global generation** — closed at AJC's curve by the dévissage route
147	   (`FiberBound.exists_bound_generated_of_isFinite_toP1`), independent of (1).  This file does
148	   not touch it; in particular nothing here makes generation uniform over extensions either.
149	-/

155	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
156	
157	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
158	
159	open Scheme
160	
161	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
162	
163	/-! ## §1. The missing instance
164	
165	`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean` gives `C_κ` the named instances `IsProper`,
166	`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1` and `GeometricallyIntegral`.  The `Ledger` curve statements bind
167	`GeometricallyIrreducible`, which is the *irreducibility* half of geometric integrality and is
168	not recovered from it by synthesis.  Mathlib has the stability instance; this names it on the
169	`baseChangeField` spelling, exactly as its three siblings do. -/
170	
171	/-- **Geometric irreducibility is stable under the field base change.**  The instance that was
172	missing from the `CurveBaseChange` stack: with it, every curve-level statement of
173	`Ledger/FiberBound.lean` applies to `C_κ` by synthesis, with no hypothesis on `κ/k`.
174	
175	Companion of `Scheme.geometricallyIntegral_hom_baseChangeField`, which is the *integral*
176	form; the `Ledger` layer binds the irreducible one. -/
177	instance Scheme.geometricallyIrreducible_hom_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ]
178	    [Algebra k κ] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
179	    GeometricallyIrreducible (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom :=
180	  MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ ‹GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom›
181	
182	/-! ## §2. The free half, witnessed at `C_κ`
183	
184	Each theorem below is the corresponding `FiberBound` curve statement applied to
185	`Scheme.baseChangeField C κ`.  The proofs are one term each: that is the point — nothing has to
186	be redone at `C_κ`, and the reason nothing has to be redone is §1, not a stability claim about
187	morphism classes.
188	
189	The `letI`/`haveI` prologue is the standing `ChiCurve` idiom (see `FiberBound.lean` §Curve): it
190	makes the ambient structure morphism of `C_κ` definitionally its bundle map, so the smoothness
191	binder that `divisorSheaf` needs transfers by `inferInstanceAs`. -/
192	
193	section FreeHalf
194	
195	variable [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
196	
197	/-- **Bounded `H¹` vanishing at `C_κ`, for every field extension `κ/k`** (the free half of
198	extension-uniformity, witnessed): a degree threshold exists over `κ`.
199	
200	The quantifier order is the whole content, and it is the *weak* one: `κ` comes first, then `b`.
201	Read `UniformVanishing` below for the strong order, which this does **not** give. -/
202	theorem vanishing_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
203	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
204	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
205	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
206	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
207	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
208	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
209	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
210	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) 1) :=
211	  exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_curve (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)
212	
213	/-- **Exact Riemann–Roch at `C_κ`, for every field extension `κ/k`**:
214	`h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1 − genus C_κ + deg_κ D` above a threshold over `κ`.
215	
216	Note the genus on the right is `genus C_κ`, taken over `κ`, **not** `genus C`.  Replacing it by
217	`genus C` is exactly the scalar identity §3 isolates, and it is not available here. -/
218	theorem riemannRoch_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
219	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
220	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
221	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
222	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
223	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
224	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
225	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
226	      (Sheaf.h0 ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) : ℤ)
227	        = 1 - genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) + CurveDivisor.deg κ D :=
228	  exists_bound_h0_eq_genus_curve (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)
229	
230	/-! ### The χ of `C_κ` is `1 − genus C_κ`
231	
232	The step that makes the decomposition of `b(κ)` in the module docstring a computation rather
233	than an estimate.  It is `ChiCurve.chi_moduleKSheaf` at `C_κ` with the genus name corrected by
234	`GenusBridge.ledgerGenus_eq_genus`; both fire at `C_κ` only because of §1. -/
235	
236	/-- **`χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = 1 − genus C_κ`.**  Isolated because it is what pins the `κ`-dependence of
237	the vanishing threshold to the genus *and nothing else on the `χ` side*: the residual
238	`κ`-dependence of `b(κ)` sits entirely in `deg_κ D₀(κ)`. -/
239	theorem chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChangeField (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
240	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
241	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
242	    Sheaf.chi ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.moduleKSheaf κ)
243	      = 1 - (genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) : ℤ) := by
244	  letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
245	    .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
246	  rw [chi_moduleKSheaf (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ),
247	    ledgerGenus_eq_genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ)]
248	
249	end FreeHalf
250	
251	/-! ## §3. The open half: named, and reduced to two explicit inputs
252	
253	`UniformVanishing` states the strong quantifier order — `b` before `κ` — as a definition, so
254	that a consumer can hypothesise it and so that the order is inspectable rather than buried in a
255	docstring.  It is **not proved**.
256	
257	`uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant` reduces it to the two inputs the module
258	docstring names.  The reduction itself is unconditional: no vanishing hypothesis, no finiteness
259	supplied by the caller, and no appeal to Serre duality (which this workspace does not have). -/
260	
261	section OpenHalf
262	
263	variable [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
264	
265	/-- **Extension-uniform bounded vanishing**, the statement.  One threshold `b`, chosen before
266	any field, serving every finite or infinite extension `κ/k` simultaneously.
267	
268	Contrast `vanishing_baseChangeField`, which is the same body with the quantifiers swapped:
269	there `κ` is fixed first and `b` may depend on it.  That one is a theorem; this one is open. -/
270	def UniformVanishing : Prop :=
271	  ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
272	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
273	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
274	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
275	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
276	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
277	    ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
278	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
279	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) 1)
280	
281	/-- **A uniform base-divisor datum**: one degree bound `d` such that over *every* extension
282	`κ/k` some divisor of degree `≤ d` already has vanishing `H¹`.
283	
284	This is input (2) of the reduction, and it is the genuinely open one.  Over a single `κ`,
285	`FiberBound.exists_base_subsingleton_of_isFinite_toP1` supplies such a `D₀` — namely `n₀ • F` —
286	but with no control of `deg_κ D₀` as `κ` varies, because `n₀(κ)` is chosen by a Noetherian
287	stabilization re-run at each base field. -/
288	def UniformBaseDivisor (d : ℤ) : Prop :=
289	  ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
290	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
291	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
292	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
293	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
294	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
295	    ∃ D₀ : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
296	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D₀) 1)
297	        ∧ CurveDivisor.deg κ D₀ ≤ d
298	
299	/-- **The reduction** (★): extension-uniform vanishing follows from a uniform base-divisor
300	degree bound together with base-field invariance of the genus, and the uniform threshold is
301	then simply `d + g`.
302	
303	Both hypotheses are needed and neither implies the other; see the module docstring for where
304	each stands.  The proof is the monotonicity observation and nothing more: the explicit bound of
305	`DegreeVanishing.subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge` at `C_κ` is
306	`deg_κ D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪_{C_κ}) = deg_κ D₀ + genus C_κ ≤ d + g`, so a `D` of degree `≥ d + g`
307	clears it. -/
308	theorem uniformVanishing_of_uniform_base_of_genus_invariant {d : ℤ} {g : ℕ}
309	    (hbase : UniformBaseDivisor C d)
310	    (hgenus : ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ],
311	      genus (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ) = g) :
312	    UniformVanishing C := by
313	  refine ⟨d + (g : ℤ), fun κ _ _ => ?_⟩
314	  letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
315	    .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
316	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
317	      ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
318	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
319	  intro D hD
320	  obtain ⟨D₀, hvan, hdeg⟩ := hbase κ
321	  have hchi : Sheaf.chi ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.moduleKSheaf κ) = 1 - (g : ℤ) := by
322	    rw [chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChangeField C κ, hgenus κ]
323	  refine subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge κ hvan D ?_
324	  rw [hchi]
325	  omega
326	
327	/-! ### Non-vacuity: the degree half-space is never empty
328	
329	A `∀ D, b ≤ deg D → …` statement is worth nothing if no divisor ever reaches degree `b`; it would
330	then be true for large `b` by having no instances, and `UniformVanishing` would be trivially
331	satisfiable.  This rules that out: one closed point of positive residue degree makes `deg`
332	unbounded above, so every degree half-space contains divisors.
333	
334	The hypothesis is the honest one — `residueDeg` positivity at a single point — rather than a
335	claim that AJC witnesses it at the challenge curve, which is a separate question and is not
336	asserted here. -/
337	
338	/-- **Degrees are unbounded above**, given one closed point of positive residue degree: for every
339	`b` there is a divisor of degree at least `b`, namely a large multiple of that point
340	(`deg (n • x) = n · [κ(x) : K]`).
341	
342	This is what makes the bounded-vanishing statements of this file and of `DegreeVanishing`
343	non-vacuous rather than true-by-emptiness. -/
344	theorem exists_deg_ge {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
345	    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X] {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X)
346	    (hpos : 0 < X.residueDeg K x) (b : ℤ) :
347	    ∃ D : X.CurveDivisor, b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K D := by
348	  refine ⟨CurveDivisor.single hx (max b 0), ?_⟩
349	  rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx]
350	  have h1 : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by exact_mod_cast hpos
351	  have h0 : (0 : ℤ) ≤ max b 0 := le_max_right _ _
352	  calc b ≤ max b 0 := le_max_left _ _
353	    _ = max b 0 * 1 := by ring
354	    _ ≤ max b 0 * (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h1 h0
355	
356	omit [IsProper C.hom] in
357	/-- The uniform statement is **strictly stronger** than the per-field one, in the only sense
358	that can be stated without proving either: it implies the per-field conclusion at every `κ`.
359	Recorded so that a consumer cannot mistake `vanishing_baseChangeField` for it.
360	
361	The `omit [IsProper C.hom]` is informative rather than cosmetic: the implication is pure
362	quantifier weakening — instantiate the single `b` at each `κ` — so it needs no properness, and
363	the linter caught that.  It confirms the two statements differ *only* in quantifier order, with
364	no geometry in between. -/
365	theorem vanishing_baseChangeField_of_uniformVanishing (h : UniformVanishing C)
366	    (κ : Type u) [Field κ] [Algebra k κ] :
367	    letI : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
368	      .ofHom (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom
369	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
370	        ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of κ)) :=
371	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).hom)
372	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : (Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.CurveDivisor,
373	      b ≤ CurveDivisor.deg κ D →
374	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((Scheme.baseChangeField C κ).left.divisorSheaf κ D) 1) := by
375	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := h
376	  exact ⟨b, hb κ⟩
377	
378	end OpenHalf
379	
380	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# `H¹` base-field invariance and base-field invariance of the genus (W5-X3)

For the challenge curve `C` over a field `k` and a field extension `K/k`
(`[Field K] [Algebra k K]`), this file proves *cohomology commutes with base change* for
the structure sheaf **from the absolute curve**: on the Rebuild carriers
(`Sheaf.HModule (·.moduleKSheaf ·) n`, two-cover Čech-definitional),

* `H⁰(C, 𝒪) ⊗[k] K ≃ₗ[K] H⁰(C_K, 𝒪)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.h0BaseFieldEquiv`),
* `H¹(C, 𝒪) ⊗[k] K ≃ₗ[K] H¹(C_K, 𝒪)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.h1BaseFieldEquiv`),

and deduces that **the genus is invariant under base field extension**
(`AlgebraicGeometry.genus_baseField`): the genus of `C_K = (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left`,
viewed as a legal curve over `K` through the `Curve.BaseChangeInstances` stack
(`baseChangeBundle C K`), equals `genus C`. The dimension count is scalar-identity-first
(W12 discipline): the one `finrank` identity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_h1_baseField`, with the `= genus C` form
`AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus` for the Wave-5 tangent count
(`dim T₀(J_k̄) = genus C`).

The engine is the flat/free cohomology-and-base-change mechanism of the landed
`Cohomology.RelativeH1BaseChange` (w4-2), run once more with the *absolute* curve as
source — NOT Mumford II.5 (no semicontinuity, no Exchange): the two-term Čech complex of
an affine two-cover base-changes termwise by the landed free identification
`relSectionsBaseChange` (`Γ(C, V) ⊗[k] R ≃ₗ[R] Γ(C_R, V_R)`), and `H¹` is its cokernel,
which commutes with any base change by right-exactness
(`LinearMap.quotRangeBaseChangeEquiv`). The intermediate statements are proved for an
arbitrary commutative `k`-algebra `R` (the `k → R` legs of the CBC ladder; the tower legs
`R → R'` are the landed `relH1BaseChange`), so the dual-numbers lane (`R = k[ε]`) can
consume them as well.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPullbackSection_resHom` — pullback of sections to the relative
  curve commutes with restriction.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.curveDiffBaseChange` — **CBC-1 (`k → R`, the commuting square)**:
  the base change of the absolute two-cover restriction-difference map is carried to the
  relative difference map under the term equivalences.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.curveH1CokBaseChange` — **CBC-2 (`i = 1`), cokernel form**:
  `R ⊗[k] H1Cok k C ≃ₗ[R] H1Cok R C_R`, with the computation rule
  `curveH1CokBaseChange_tmul_mk`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.curveH1BaseChange` — **CBC-2 (`i = 1`) on the cohomology carriers**:
  `R ⊗[k] H¹(C, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[R] H¹(C_R, 𝒪)` for every commutative `k`-algebra `R`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.curveH0BaseChange` — the degree-zero analogue, free of charge from
  `relSectionsBaseChange` at `V = ⊤` (`C` proper makes `⊤` qcqs).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.h1BaseFieldEquiv`, `AlgebraicGeometry.h0BaseFieldEquiv` — the
  headline field-extension statements, keyed on the `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` spelling of
  `Curve.BaseChangeInstances`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_h1_baseField`, `AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_h0_baseField`,
  `AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus` — the scalar `finrank` identities.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus_baseField` — `genus (baseChangeBundle C K) = genus C`.

## Implementation notes

The `k`-module structure on the absolute sections `Γ(C.left, V)` appears in two
definitionally equal presentations: `Scheme.overModule` under the
`letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom` of the frozen `genus` spelling (the

32	  with the curve pullbacks (`relSectionsMap_pullback`), it intertwines the structure

34	  semilinearity `relSectionsMap_smul`), and it commutes with restriction

115	    | add x y hx hy => rw [smul_add, map_add, map_add, hx, hy, map_add, map_add, smul_add]

118	        TensorProduct.comm_tmul, Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul,
119	        Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul, map_mul, Scheme.overModule_smul_def]
120	      exact mul_left_comm _ _ _

122	/-- The base-change equivalence on a pure tensor: `a ⊗ s` goes to the structure
123	pullback of `a` times the pullback of `s` along the first projection (equivalently,
124	by `Scheme.overModule_smul_def`, to the `Scheme.overModule` action of `a` on the

127	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set C.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set C.left))
128	    (a : R) (s : Γ(C.left, V)) :
129	    relSectionsBaseChange C R hV hV' (a ⊗ₜ s) =
130	      (relCurve C R).overAlgebraMap R ((fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) a *
131	        relPullbackSection C R V s := by
132	  change Over.sectionsBaseChange C R hV hV'
133	    (TensorProduct.comm k R Γ(C.left, V) (a ⊗ₜ s)) = _
134	  rw [TensorProduct.comm_tmul, Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul]
135	  exact mul_comm _ _

import Mathlib

/-!
# Base change of sections along the projection `C ⊗ Spec A ⟶ C`

For an object `C` of `Over (Spec k)` (`k` a field), a commutative `k`-algebra `A`, and a
quasi-compact quasi-separated open `V ⊆ C.left`, this file identifies the sections of the
base change `(C ⊗ Spec A).left` over the preimage `V_A := (fst C (Spec A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V` of
`V` under the first projection with the tensor product of the sections over `V`:

`Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+* Γ((C ⊗ overSpec k A).left, V_A)`

(`AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsBaseChange`), sending `s ⊗ a` to the product of the two
pullbacks (`sectionsBaseChange_tmul`), compatibly with restriction along `W ≤ V`
(`sectionsBaseChange_naturality`). Here `C ⊗ T` is the cartesian-monoidal product of
`Over (Spec k)`, realized by `Limits.pullback`; the single bridge lemma between the two
languages is `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPullback_left`.

This is brick 1 of the separatedness ledger (design §4.4): one brick, three consumers —
étale separatedness (arbitrary `A`), the dual-numbers tangent engine (`A = k[ε]`), and the
χ-ledger under field extension (`A = K`). Hence the statements are for an arbitrary
commutative `k`-algebra `A`, and `V` is allowed to be any quasi-compact quasi-separated
open (e.g. the intersection of two affines of the curve), not just an affine one.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPullback_left` — the bridge: for `X T : Over S`, the scheme-level
  square `(fst X T).left, (snd X T).left, X.hom, T.hom` is a pullback.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.overSpec k A` — `Spec A` as an object of `Over (Spec k)`, together with
  the instance `Flat (overSpec k A).hom` (automatic over a field).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsAlgebra` — the `k`-algebra structure on `Γ(X.left, V)` by
  restriction of scalars along the structure morphism. Deliberately **not** a global instance
  (house rule, cf. `Scheme.overModule`); consumers activate it with
  `attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.resAlgHom` — restriction of sections as a `k`-algebra homomorphism.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_sections_of_isAffineOpen`,
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_sections` — the master pushout squares on sections, for
  an arbitrary test object `T` with `T.left` affine (affine `V` needs no flatness; qcqs `V`
  needs `[Flat T.hom]`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections` — the same square with the
  `Γ(Spec k, ⊤)`/`Γ(Spec A, ⊤)` corners replaced by `k` and `A`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsBaseChangeIso`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsBaseChange`
  — the comparison isomorphism (in `CommRingCat`, resp. as a ring equivalence), with the
  computation rules `sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one`, `sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul`,
  `sectionsBaseChange_tmul` and the restriction-naturality
  `sectionsBaseChange_naturality`.

## Implementation notes

The heavy lifting is mathlib's `pushoutSection` API
(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Flat.lean`): for a pullback square of schemes the
canonical map `Γ(X, Uₓ) ⊗[Γ(S, Uₛ)] Γ(T, Uₜ) ⟶ Γ(X ×ₛ T, ...)` is an isomorphism for
affine `Uₛ, Uₜ` and qcqs `Uₓ` when `T ⟶ S` is flat — which over a field is automatic.
This file only supplies the Over-category bridge, the corner bookkeeping (`ΓSpecIso`), and
the tensor-product face.

/-!
# `H⁰` commutes with affine base change, in the form the B3 gate consumes

`Picard/RigidPushforwardAffineDescent.lean` reduces the second field of the campaign gate
`Scheme.HasRigidPushforward` — `Scheme.RigidPushforwardBaseChange` — to the single module-level
statement `Adelic.RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange`: bijectivity of the canonical
`Γ(Spec A', ⊤) ⊗_{Γ(Spec A, ⊤)} Γ(C_A, L) → Γ(C_{A'}, g'^* L)`.  This file proves that
statement.

## §1, the general theorem

`exists_gammaBaseChange_of_kerPure` takes a cartesian square

```
  X' --g'--> X
  |f'        |f
  v          v
  Y' --g---> Y
```

with `Y`, `Y'` affine and `g'` affine, a bundled 2-affine cover `𝒰` of `X`, a quasi-coherent `M`,
and the Čech `H⁰`-purity hypothesis `hker` (the kernel base-change map of the two-term Čech
difference `d = 𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase f M` is bijective for every `Γ(Y, ⊤)`-algebra `B`), and
produces the canonical comparison

`Γ(Y', ⊤) ⊗_{Γ(Y, ⊤)} Γ(f_* M, ⊤) ≅ Γ(f'_* (g'^* M), ⊤)`, `b ⊗ x ↦ b · baseMap x`.

It is a sandwich of three existing pieces: the sheaf condition on both sides
(`AffineCoverMVSquare.globalSectionsEquivKerModuleSectionDiffBase`, which identifies `Γ` with
`ker d`), the affine-base-change Čech square on kernels
(`Adelic.exists_kerChartTensorEquiv`, `Picard/RigidPushforwardChartBaseChange.lean`), and the
`pushforward`-versus-`baseSections` dictionary at the two tops
(`Scheme.Modules.pushforwardTopEquivBaseSections`).  The only computation is that the resulting
map does send `b ⊗ x` to `b · baseMap x`, which is the restriction naturality
`pullback_app_isoTensor_baseMap_res'` on each of the two charts.

Note what is *not* assumed: `f` is arbitrary — in the application it is the proper, emphatically
non-affine family `q : C_A ⟶ Spec A`, which is exactly the case
`Picard/RigidPushforwardFrontier.lean` reports as having no infrastructure.

Sources: Stacks 01HQ, 02KG at `i = 0`; Mumford, *Abelian Varieties*, II §5; EGA III 7.7.5.

/-!
## Sections of fibered products

Suppose we are given the following cartesian square:
```
Y --g-→ X
|       |
iY      iX
↓       |
T --f-→ S
```
Let `Uₛ` be an open of `S`, `Uₓ` and `Uₜ` be opens of `X` and `T` mapping into `Uₛ`.
There is a canonical map `Γ(X, Uₓ) ⊗[Γ(S, Uₛ)] Γ(T, Uₜ) ⟶ Γ(X ×ₛ T, pr₁ ⁻¹ Uₓ ∩ pr₂ ⁻¹ Uₜ)`.

We show that this map is
1. `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isAffineOpen`:
  bijective when `Uₛ`, `Uₜ`, and `Uₓ` are all affine.
2. `mono_pushoutSection_of_isCompact_of_flat_right`:
  injective when `Uₛ`, `Uₜ` are affine, `Uₓ` is compact, and `f` is flat.
3. `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`:
  bijective when `Uₛ`, `Uₜ` are affine, `Uₓ` is qcqs, and `f` is flat.
4. `mono_pushoutSection_of_isCompact_of_flat_right_of_ringHomFlat`:
  injective when `Uₛ` is affine, `Uₜ` is compact, `Uₓ` is qcqs, `f` is flat,
  and `Γ(T, Uₜ)` is flat over `Γ(S, Uₛ)` (typically true when `S = Spec k`.)
5. `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isCompact_of_flat_right_of_ringHomFlat`:
  bijective when `Uₛ` is affine, `Uₜ` and `Uₓ` are qcqs, `f` is flat,
  and `Γ(T, Uₜ)` is flat over `Γ(S, Uₛ)` (typically true when `S = Spec k`.)

-/

variable {X Y S T : Scheme.{u}} {f : T ⟶ S} {g : Y ⟶ X} {iX : X ⟶ S} {iY : Y ⟶ T}
  (H : IsPullback g iY iX f)
  {US : S.Opens} {UT : T.Opens}
  {UX : X.Opens} (hUST : UT ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ US) (hUSX : UX ≤ iX ⁻¹ᵁ US)
  {UY : Y.Opens} (hUY : UY = g ⁻¹ᵁ UX ⊓ iY ⁻¹ᵁ UT)

/-- The canonical map `Γ(X, Uₓ) ⊗[Γ(S, Uₛ)] Γ(T, Uₜ) ⟶ Γ(X ×ₛ T, pr₁ ⁻¹ Uₓ ∩ pr₂ ⁻¹ Uₜ)`.
This is an isomorphism under various circumstances. -/
abbrev pushoutSection : pushout (iX.appLE US UX hUSX) (f.appLE US UT hUST) ⟶ Γ(Y, UY) :=
  pushout.desc (g.appLE UX UY (by simp [*])) (iY.appLE UT UY (by simp [*]))
    (by simp only [Scheme.Hom.appLE_comp_appLE, H.w])

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
lemma isIso_pushoutSection_iff :
    IsIso (pushoutSection H hUST hUSX hUY) ↔ IsPushout (iX.appLE US UX hUSX) (f.appLE US UT hUST)
      (g.appLE UX UY (by simp [*])) (iY.appLE UT UY (by simp [*])) :=
  ⟨fun _ ↦ .of_iso (.of_hasPushout _ _) (.refl _) (.refl _) (.refl _)
    (asIso (pushoutSection H hUST hUSX hUY)) (by simp) (by simp) (by simp) (by simp),
    fun h ↦ inferInstanceAs (IsIso h.isoPushout.inv)⟩

set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in
attribute [local simp] IsAffineOpen.isoSpec_hom in
attribute [local simp← ] Scheme.Hom.resLE_eq_morphismRestrict in
lemma isIso_pushoutSection_of_isAffineOpen (hUS : IsAffineOpen US) (hUT : IsAffineOpen UT)
    (hUX : IsAffineOpen UX) : IsIso (pushoutSection H hUST hUSX hUY) := by
  refine (isIso_pushoutSection_iff ..).mpr (IsPullback.of_map_of_faithful Scheme.Spec ?_).unop
  have : IsAffine _ := hUS
  have : IsAffine _ := hUT
  have : IsAffine _ := hUX
  have hUY' : IsAffineOpen UY :=
    .of_isIso (Scheme.Hom.isPullback_resLE H hUST hUSX hUY).isoPullback.hom
  exact .of_iso (Scheme.Hom.isPullback_resLE H hUST hUSX hUY).flip hUY'.isoSpec hUT.isoSpec
    hUX.isoSpec hUS.isoSpec (by simp) (by simp) (by simp) (by simp)

    (f.flat_appLE hUS hUT _)

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.Basic

8	/-!
9	# Global sections of a proper geometrically integral scheme over a field
10	
11	The keystone of the curve substrate: for a scheme `X` proper and geometrically integral over a
12	field `K`, the structure map induces an isomorphism `K ≅ Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.
13	
14	* `AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`:
15	  the honest general form — `f.appTop : Γ(Spec K, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤)` is bijective.
16	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral` and the bundle instance
17	  `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_hom_appTop_of_geometricallyReduced`: the instance-friendly forms.
18	
19	## Proof sketch
20	
21	Write `A := Γ(X, ⊤)`. By Mathlib's properness facts (`isField_of_universallyClosed`,
22	`finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`), `A` is a field, finite over `K`. Base change `f` along
23	`Spec A ⟶ Spec K`: the total space `X_A` is again proper and geometrically integral over the
24	field `A`, so `Γ(X_A, ⊤)` is a field as well. Flat base change of sections
25	(`isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right`) exhibits `Γ(X_A, ⊤)` as the pushout
26	`A ⊗[K] A`. A pushout of a field extension along itself being a field forces `K ⟶ A` to be an
27	*epimorphism* of rings (`CommRingCat.epi_of_isPushout_of_isField`: the codiagonal
28	`A ⊗[K] A ⟶ A` is injective, being a ring map out of a field, and surjective, being split by
29	`inl`; hence `inl` is an isomorphism and the two coprojections agree). A finite ring
30	epimorphism is surjective (`RingHom.surjective_of_epi_of_finite`), and any ring map out of a
31	field is injective.
32	
33	Geometric reducedness enters only through `GeometricallyIntegral`; for the curve bundle of the
34	challenge it is supplied by "smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced", proved elsewhere in this project.
35	-/
36	
37	set_option autoImplicit false
38	
39	universe u
40	
41	open CategoryTheory Limits
42	
43	namespace CommRingCat
44	
45	/-- If a pushout square of commutative rings has isomorphic legs (`e : C ≅ B` intertwining
46	`ψ` and `φ`) and its pushout `D` is a field, then `φ` is an epimorphism.
47	
48	This is the classical "diagonal" criterion: the codiagonal `μ : D ⟶ B` determined by
49	`𝟙 B` and `e.hom` is injective (a ring map out of a field into a nontrivial ring) and split
50	surjective, hence an isomorphism; so `inl = e.inv ≫ inr`, which makes `φ` epi. -/
51	lemma epi_of_isPushout_of_isField {A B C D : CommRingCat.{u}}
52	    {φ : A ⟶ B} {ψ : A ⟶ C} {inl : B ⟶ D} {inr : C ⟶ D}
53	    (H : IsPushout φ ψ inl inr) (hD : IsField D) [Nontrivial B]
54	    (e : C ≅ B) (he : ψ ≫ e.hom = φ) : Epi φ := by
55	  letI : Field D := hD.toField
56	  -- the codiagonal
57	  let μ : D ⟶ B := H.desc (𝟙 B) e.hom (by rw [Category.comp_id, he])
58	  have hμinl : inl ≫ μ = 𝟙 B := H.inl_desc _ _ _
59	  have hμinr : inr ≫ μ = e.hom := H.inr_desc _ _ _
60	  have : IsIso μ := by
61	    refine (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective μ).mpr ⟨μ.hom.injective, fun b ↦ ⟨inl b, ?_⟩⟩
62	    simpa using congr($(hμinl) b)
63	  -- the two coprojections agree up to `e`
64	  have key : e.inv ≫ inr = inl := by
65	    rw [← cancel_mono μ, Category.assoc, hμinr, hμinl, Iso.inv_hom_id]
66	  refine ⟨fun {W} u v huv ↦ ?_⟩
67	  have w : φ ≫ u = ψ ≫ (e.hom ≫ v) := by
68	    rw [← Category.assoc, he]; exact huv
69	  calc u = inl ≫ H.desc u (e.hom ≫ v) w := (H.inl_desc _ _ _).symm
70	    _ = e.inv ≫ inr ≫ H.desc u (e.hom ≫ v) w := by rw [← Category.assoc, key]
71	    _ = e.inv ≫ e.hom ≫ v := by rw [H.inr_desc]
72	    _ = v := by rw [Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
73	
74	end CommRingCat
75	
76	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
77	
78	/-- Bundled variant of `AlgebraicGeometry.isField_of_universallyClosed`: if `X` is an integral
79	scheme, universally closed over the spectrum of a (bundled) commutative ring `R` that is a
80	field, then `Γ(X, ⊤)` is a field. -/
81	theorem isField_of_universallyClosed_of_isField {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (hR : IsField R)
82	    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec R) [IsIntegral X] [UniversallyClosed f] :
83	    IsField Γ(X, ⊤) := by
84	  let F := (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).inv ≫ f.appTop
85	  have : F.hom.IsIntegral := by
86	    apply RingHom.isIntegral_respectsIso.2 (e := (Scheme.ΓSpecIso R).symm.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv)
87	    exact isIntegral_appTop_of_universallyClosed f
88	  algebraize [F.hom]
89	  exact isField_of_isIntegral_of_isField' hR
90	
91	/-- **Global sections of a proper geometrically integral scheme over a field.**
92	If `X` is proper and geometrically integral over a field `K`, then the map on global sections
93	`Γ(Spec K, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤)` induced by the structure morphism is bijective; informally,
94	`Γ(X, 𝒪_X) = K`. -/
95	theorem bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral
96	    {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
97	    [IsProper f] [GeometricallyIntegral f] :
98	    Function.Bijective f.appTop := by
99	  have hX : IsIntegral X := GeometricallyIntegral.isIntegral_of_subsingleton f
100	  -- `A := Γ(X, ⊤)` is a field, finite over `K`.
101	  have hA : IsField Γ(X, ⊤) := isField_of_universallyClosed K f
102	  letI : Field Γ(X, ⊤) := hA.toField
103	  letI : Field Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) :=
104	    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv.toMulEquiv.isField
105	      (Field.toIsField K)).toField
106	  refine ⟨f.appTop.hom.injective, ?_⟩
107	  -- Surjectivity: `f.appTop` is a finite epimorphism.
108	  suffices h : Epi f.appTop from
109	    RingHom.surjective_of_epi_of_finite f.appTop (finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed K f)
110	  -- Base change to `Spec Γ(X, ⊤)`.
111	  set q : Spec Γ(X, ⊤) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K) :=
112	    Spec.map ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).inv ≫ f.appTop) with hq
113	  -- The total space of the base change is integral, so its global sections form a field.
114	  have hsub : Subsingleton ↥(Spec Γ(X, ⊤)) :=
115	    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum Γ(X, ⊤)))
116	  have hYint : IsIntegral (pullback f q) :=
117	    GeometricallyIntegral.isIntegral_of_subsingleton (pullback.snd f q)
118	  have hUC : UniversallyClosed (pullback.snd f q) :=
119	    MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ inferInstance
120	  have hD : IsField Γ(pullback f q, ⊤) :=
121	    isField_of_universallyClosed_of_isField hA (pullback.snd f q)
122	  -- Flat base change of global sections: the pushout square.
123	  have hUST : (⊤ : (Spec Γ(X, ⊤)).Opens) ≤ q ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top q).ge
124	  have hUSX : (⊤ : X.Opens) ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top f).ge
125	  have hUY : (⊤ : (pullback f q).Opens) =
126	      pullback.fst f q ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ ⊓ pullback.snd f q ⁻¹ᵁ ⊤ := by simp
127	  have hCS : CompactSpace X := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f
128	  have hQS : QuasiSeparatedSpace X := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated f
129	  have hiso := isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right
130	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f q) hUST hUSX hUY
131	    (isAffineOpen_top _) (isAffineOpen_top _)
132	    (by simpa using CompactSpace.isCompact_univ)
133	    (by simpa using isQuasiSeparated_univ)
134	  have hpo := (isIso_pushoutSection_iff
135	    (IsPullback.of_hasPullback f q) hUST hUSX hUY).mp hiso
136	  -- The two legs of the pushout square agree up to `ΓSpecIso`.
137	  have hcompat : q.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUST ≫ (Scheme.ΓSpecIso Γ(X, ⊤)).hom = f.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUSX := by
138	    have h₁ : q.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUST = q.appTop := Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app q
139	    have h₂ : f.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUSX = f.appTop := Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app f
140	    rw [h₁, h₂, hq, Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
141	  have hepi : Epi (f.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUSX) :=
142	    CommRingCat.epi_of_isPushout_of_isField hpo hD (Scheme.ΓSpecIso Γ(X, ⊤)) hcompat
143	  rwa [show f.appLE ⊤ ⊤ hUSX = f.appTop from Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app f] at hepi
144	
145	/-- Instance-friendly form of
146	`AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`. -/
147	theorem isIso_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral
148	    {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
149	    [IsProper f] [GeometricallyIntegral f] :
150	    IsIso f.appTop :=
151	  (ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective _).mpr
152	    (bijective_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral f)
153	
154	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
155	
156	/-- `Γ(C, 𝒪_C) ≅ k` for the curve bundle: the structure morphism of a proper, geometrically
157	irreducible, geometrically reduced scheme over `k` induces an isomorphism on global sections.
158	
159	Geometric reducedness is a hypothesis here; for the curve bundle of the challenge it is
160	supplied by "smooth ⟹ geometrically reduced", proved elsewhere in this project. -/
161	instance isIso_hom_appTop_of_geometricallyReduced (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
162	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] :
163	    IsIso C.hom.appTop :=
164	  have : GeometricallyIntegral C.hom :=
165	    GeometricallyIntegral.of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible C.hom
166	  isIso_appTop_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral (K := k) C.hom
167	
168	section RegressionChecks
169	
170	variable {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
171	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
172	  [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]

name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
